content.question: When attaching one element to another in ConstraintLayout, what does attaching the top of element B to the bottom of element A mean?

options.text: The top edge of B will be positioned relative to the bottom edge of A
Both elements will merge into one

content.explanation: Attaching the top of one element to the bottom of another creates a vertical constraint so the second element is placed below the first.
hints: Think positions relative to each other

content.question: What is the purpose of providing an ID to a view in XML?

options.text: To uniquely identify the view so it can be referenced in code or constraints

content.explanation: An ID gives a unique identity to a component so you can reference it in code or set constraints relative to it.

content.question: If a constraint spot is already occupied, can another view attach to the same exact constraint point?

options.text: Yes, unlimited views can attach to one constraint
No, a single constraint attachment point can generally be used only once

content.explanation: The instructor notes that once a particular constraint is occupied, you cannot attach another constraint there; each connection point is used by one attachment.

content.question: What action should you take to remove only a constraint attachment (and keep the view)?

options.text: Right-click the constraint and choose delete constraint

content.explanation: You can remove the constraint attachment specifically (without deleting the component) by selecting and deleting the constraint connector, as demonstrated in the video.

content.question: Which method does the instructor use to ensure one element stays below another while moving the top element?

options.text: Attach the bottom of the lower element to the top of the upper element
Give both elements the same ID

content.explanation: By creating a constraint link between the bottom of the upper element and the top of the lower element, moving the upper element moves the lower one too.
